eips.title: Enshrined Proposer-Builder Separation
eips.summary: Builder payment edge case was the main topic; fix must land before Hoodi, but no reason to delay Sepolia.

moments.context: Justin Traglia opened the breakout on an edge case regarding builder payments, asking to discuss it without covering how it could be exploited.

Potuz explained that since the partial state transition on payload import was removed (spec change 5094), a block building on a full payload processes the previous payload's requests first — so a request containing a builder exit is processed unconditionally, before that payload's builder payments.
Justin Traglia confirmed there was no reason to delay Sepolia over it; Potuz noted it cannot be triggered there anyway.

eips.title: Increase exit and consolidation churn
eips.summary: Referenced as the basis for reducing epoch retention to 14K epochs, with general client agreement.

moments.context: Kevaundray noted that everyone seems okay with modifying retention given EIP-8061, setting it to 14K epochs, with clients free to keep more data if they wish.

eips.title: Quick Slots
eips.summary: Shorter slots feature spec discussed regarding testing approach, FOCIL prerequisites, and tooling implications.

moments.context: Barnabas asked if anyone started work on shorter slots. Nico said Lodestar has a working branch but not on the latest spec. Discussion covered whether it should be tested on top of FOCIL since timing interactions matter, and that it is a feature spec based on Heze. Justin confirmed the PR was merged.
